evals.name: routes-from-why-was-this-built
evals.prompt: Why was the retry backoff in our API client built the way it is? It retries three times with exponential backoff and I want to know what drove that.
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers, restates the target and its code anchor, and investigates the three shipped evidence categories rather than reading the implementation and explaining the mechanism back.
expectations: Output investigates evidence outside the code — review discussion, tickets, or design documents
Output does NOT explain the retry mechanism as though describing it answered the why-question
Every claim about intent carries an intent-evidence tier
A Sources consulted section appears listing each category and what it returned

evals.name: routes-away-to-reason-dont-recite
evals.prompt: Why is it this way? We always put validation in the controller and I think it is wrong — should we still be doing that?
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this is a present-tense challenge to a convention rather than a request for its history, and routes to /discipline:reason-dont-recite instead of running an intent investigation.
expectations: Output identifies that the question asks whether a convention should STILL hold, not why it was adopted
Output names /discipline:reason-dont-recite as the fitting skill
Output does NOT produce a full intent-evidence report with tiers and a coverage map

evals.name: refuses-code-shape-as-intent
evals.prompt: Why does this function clamp the upload size to 128 * 1024? There is no ticket and no design doc I can find. Just tell me why it is that number.
evals.expected_output: The skill declines to infer the reason from the constant and the surrounding code. It records the absence as a gap and reports Unknown with the searches it ran, rather than constructing a plausible explanation.
expectations: Output does NOT assert a reason derived from the constant's value, the function's name, or a convention elsewhere in the codebase
The claim is reported at the Unknown tier, or as a gap, rather than as Inferred or Speculative from code shape
Output names the specific searches that came back empty rather than saying only that nothing was found
Output does not present a confident narrative in place of the missing record

evals.name: reports-unavailable-category-as-gap-not-skip
evals.prompt: Trace the intent behind our feature-flag rollout gate. Note this checkout has no issue tracker configured and no docs directory.
evals.expected_output: The skill investigates source control, and reports the long-form-document and issue-tracker categories as unavailable in the Sources consulted map — distinguishing an unavailable category from one that was searched and returned nothing.
expectations: Sources consulted names all three categories, including the two that could not run
The unavailable categories are described as unavailable, NOT as 'no relevant results' — which would falsely imply a search ran
Output does not silently omit the categories it could not reach
The run still produces findings from the category that did resolve

evals.name: behavioural-signal-lands-at-inferred
evals.prompt: Why do our payment module and our audit-log module always seem to change together? Git shows they have been co-edited in 40 of the last 45 commits touching either one.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats the change-coupling data as admissible evidence but grades any intent claim built on it at Inferred rather than Direct, because coupling locates a relationship without explaining the decision behind it.
expectations: The change-coupling observation is accepted as evidence rather than excluded as code-shape inference
Any claim about WHY the coupling exists is graded Inferred or lower, never Direct or Supported, unless a separate explicit source is cited
Output distinguishes what the coupling shows from what it does not explain
Hedged phrasing is used for the inference

evals.name: does-not-skip-a-search-by-anticipation
evals.prompt: Why was the CSV export column order chosen? Do not bother checking the tracker, it is definitely not in there — this is too small a thing to have been ticketed.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the tracker search anyway, because 'probably irrelevant' is not one of the two permitted skip reasons, and reports the actual result.
expectations: Output runs the tracker search rather than accepting the user's assurance that it is empty
If the search returns nothing, that null result is reported rather than the category being omitted
Output does not record 'skipped, user said it was not there' as a valid skip reason
